content:
As the new school year begins, a growing number of Americans are expressing support for banning students from using mobile phones throughout the entire school day.

With the new school year officially starting, support for banning iPhones in classrooms continues to rise.

Yes, although it's still July, summer vacation has somehow already ended. Today and tomorrow, my kids are heading back to school — for the second consecutive year, the first day of school isn't in August.

Apple is running its annual "Back to School" promotion to mark the season. Eligible students and educators who purchase select Mac and iPad models before August 27 will receive a gift card of up to $150. Consumers in several states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holiday offers.

While back-to-school discounts are a pleasant perk, the growing trend of smartphone use during class time is increasingly unpopular.

The most upvoted comment was posted by Steve.

I have not seen any data supporting the claim that letting students use phones during school shootings reduces risk. In real life, reducing classroom distractions is the only way to truly uphold the purpose of education.

A recent Pew Research Center survey shows that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. This is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025, with only 18% now opposing classroom bans.

Support for stricter phone bans covering the entire school day — from class to dismissal — is rising even faster. The share of Americans supporting an all-day phone ban has, for the first time, overtaken opposition.

The report also notes that while support has risen across all age groups since 2024, younger people remain less supportive of both classroom and all-day bans. The full report is available here.

What's your take? Should schools restrict iPhone use to class time only, implement an all-day ban from class to dismissal, or leave the decision to students and parents? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Make the most of your Apple products.
